text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Daniel arap Moi invokes the Preservation of Public Security Act, giving him sweeping powers to make regulations to deal with famine.
- An 11.3 billion shilling European financing agreement signals renewed donor confidence in Kenya.
- Twelve opposition members of parliament ask President Moi to revoke the appointment of Nicholas Biwott to the cabinet.
- Influential businessman Joshua Kulei goes to court outraged by press reports associating him with a so-called Asian link in President Moi's "kitchen cabinet".
- Jordan establishes diplomatic relations with Kenya at consulate level.
- A man is sentenced to death for robbing and burning to death a man and his two grandchildren.
- The Soweto slum in a Nairobi suburb is flattened.
- Kenya's vice-president says some 2.5 million Kenyans will require famine relief in the next six months.
- A minister of state in the office of the president says the government will withdraw firearms and ammunition from homeguards. ($1=54 Kenyan shillings)
